## Not yet found / research gaps to search next run
- Partly covered 2026-10-30: SCC (R72, 2018 dissertation), mass concrete heat (R73, 2017 field study).
- Partly covered 2026-11-06: 3D printing now three lab studies (R56, R57, R132). R132 TEA quotes PLC ~$0.16/kg and limestone ~$0.038/kg (2025 e-commerce) — still not a ready-mix market cost series.
- Still open: primary ACI 318/301 code text (ACA hub R138 is secondary confirmation of inclusion); EN 197-1 official text (only secondary citations, e.g. R132).
- Partly covered 2026-10-29: shotcrete (R55), GCCA (R58, R59; no PLC-specific GCCA doc found).
- Microcracking (2026-10-30): no direct imaging of ITZ microcracks in Type IL vs OPC concrete; nothing separating limestone aggregate from filler effects in PLC; no DIC on PLC; no NIST or FHWA report specific to this.
- Mass concrete (2026-11-04, R105-R124): no field case study of a Type IL mass pour with temperature monitoring; no same-clinker adiabatic IL vs I/II comparison other than FDOT; DEF with PLC only in lab studies; no DOT other than Florida addresses Type IL in its mass spec; ACI 207 silent on Type IL. R118 (GDOT) authors/year unconfirmed.
- 2026-11-05: Added R125–R131 (FHWA PLC variability TechNote; ACI early-age HES/PLC; ASCE nanosilica carbonation; PINN hydration-heat surrogate; Type IL UHPC+calcined clay; IU Ferguson ACA case; OKDOT Type IL(10) QPL).
- 2026-11-06: Added R132–R139 (Nature Comm CNF+LF printable PLC; Euclid Type IL contractor guide; crystalline Type IL article; WDM Type IL pavement forensic; Masten NCC PLC variability/steering; CP Tech paving carbon guide; ACA blended-cements hub; WVDOH Type 1L approved mill list). WDM forensic is strong field evidence that early Iowa pavement distress tracked construction response, not Type IL chemistry. Braun Intertec 10-PLC fresh-properties study (R136) still pending Fall 2026 NCC presentation.

### Four-axis taxonomy and takeaways

#### Cement and binder families
- binder-portland — Binder · Portland I–V and air-entraining: Seeded: Types I, II, III, V and IA/IIA/IIIA; Type IV retained as historical low-heat classification, not implied current local availability. R28 now describes four current basic types. Verify adopted edition before specifying. Sources: R28, R140.
- binder-blended — Binder · IL / IS / IP / ternary and performance cements: Seeded: preserve IL research and add slag/pozzolan/ternary and C1157 performance route. C595-26 Type IC and changing composition require edition-specific checks; blend labels are not universal performance guarantees. Sources: R28, R37, R39, R40, R138, R140.
- binder-international — Binder · International CEM I–VI and regional classifications: Catalogue-level seed only: CEM I–V common cements are associated with EN 197-1; CEM II/C-M and CEM VI with EN 197-5. Not one interchangeable CEM I–VI standard; full normative text and global crosswalk remain gaps. Sources: R58, R149, R150.
- binder-cac-csa — Binder · Calcium aluminate / calcium sulfoaluminate: Seeded FAQ, preview and nonstructural mortar abstract. CAC and CSA are different chemistries; refractory, conversion, sulfate balance, curing and structural approvals need separate qualification. No general structural design guide added. Sources: R140, R141, R142.
- binder-specialty — Binder · Rapid-set / expansive / shrinkage-compensating: Foundational preview discusses rapid-hardening and controlled early expansion. Rapid set is not synonymous with high early strength; shrinkage compensation requires restraint and curing design. Current C845/C1600 requirements not verified. Sources: R140, R141, R142.
- binder-white-masonry — Binder · White / colored / masonry / mortar / plastic: Seeded historical specialty classification and manufacturer white masonry page. Distinguish cement from mortar, pigment from binder chemistry, C91 masonry from C1329 mortar and C1328 plastic cement; latest normative clauses and independent comparisons remain gaps. Sources: R140, R147.
- binder-well — Binder · Oil-well and geothermal cement: Seeded API 10A context from 2016 preview and DOE geothermal research. Downhole temperature, pressure, fluids, thermal cycling, casing bond and seal integrity govern qualification; latest API/ISO normative editions not reviewed. Sources: R140, R144.
- binder-activated — Binder · Alkali-activated / geopolymer: Initial abstract-level coverage only. Activator, precursor, curing, shrinkage and leaching/efflorescence need system-specific testing. Geopolymer is not a blanket synonym for every alkali-activated binder; structural field/code coverage thin. Sources: R142, R144.
- binder-lc3 — Binder · Calcined-clay / limestone / LC3 low-clinker systems: Seeded EPFL project page plus preserved IL/UHPC research. Project up-to-40% CO2 claim is conditional; clay mineralogy, calcination, sulfate optimization and functional-unit LCA matter. LC3 is not simply Type IL with added filler. Sources: R129, R143.
- binder-magnesium-carbonatable — Binder · Magnesium-based and carbonatable binders: Reviews distinguish Mg silicate/carbonate/oxysalt and carbonatable calcium-silicate systems. CO2 curing differs from injecting CO2 into normal concrete; steel passivation, water resistance, energy and carbon accounting remain limitations. Sources: R145, R146.

#### SCMs and additions
- scm-slag — SCM / addition · Slag cement: Foundational seed: Slag cement has source-dependent latent hydraulic activity; review grades, sulfate resistance, early strength and curing, not just replacement percentage. Sources: R167, R24.
- scm-flyash — SCM / addition · Fly ash / coal ash: Foundational seed: Fly ash chemistry and source variability affect reactivity and air/admixture demand; current supply and reclaimed ash qualification need further sources. Sources: R167, R24.
- scm-natural — SCM / addition · Natural pozzolans: Foundational seed: Natural pozzolans require mineralogy, reactivity and durability qualification; R103 adds only a limited Type IL early-age study. Sources: R167, R24.
- scm-clay — SCM / addition · Calcined clay / metakaolin: Foundational seed: Calcined clay is an SCM; LC3 is a blended binder system using it. Clay quality and process energy are important. Sources: R167, R24.
- scm-silica — SCM / addition · Silica fume: Foundational seed: Silica fume appears in UHPC/high-performance systems; dispersion, rheology and curing need mix-specific control. Sources: R167, R24.
- scm-limestone — SCM / addition · Limestone fillers and inert fines: Foundational seed: Limestone filler is separately classified from pozzolanic SCMs; packing/nucleation and carboaluminate effects do not make every filler a pozzolan. Sources: R59, R132.
- scm-emerging — SCM / addition · Emerging / alternative SCMs: Gap: Coverage gap: harvested ash, ground glass, biomass ash, mine residues and other alternatives lack individual verified standards/field sources in this pass. Sources: coverage gap — no dedicated source yet.

#### Concrete families and applications
- concrete-structural — Concrete · Normal-weight / reinforced / prestressed: Seeded / partial: Seeded general use, IL prestressed study and grout overview; broad structural detailing and current codes are not yet indexed. Sources: R28, R31, R162.
- concrete-hpc — Concrete · High-strength / HPC / UHPC: Seeded / partial: Separate compressive strength from broader performance and fiber-dependent UHPC tensile behavior; foundational sources are not latest design provisions. Sources: R155, R169, R129.
- concrete-scc — Concrete · Self-consolidating concrete: Seeded / partial: Flowability plus stability; fresh-property tests and placement trials remain necessary. Sources: R173, R72.
- concrete-fibers — Concrete · Fiber-reinforced concrete and composites: Seeded / partial: Synthetic-fiber guidance plus UHPC report; steel/glass/basalt fibers, ECC and FRC structural design still need dedicated coverage. Sources: R164, R155.
- concrete-lightweight — Concrete · Lightweight aggregate concrete: Seeded / partial: Structural lightweight aggregate concrete is not interchangeable with foamed fill. Sources: R172.
- concrete-heavyweight — Concrete · Heavyweight / shielding / ballast: Seeded / partial: Density and form pressure/handling require special consideration; shielding design outside reviewed source. Sources: R148.
- concrete-cellular — Concrete · Cellular / foamed / aerated: Seeded / partial: Geotechnical foamed/cellular guide seeded; autoclaved aerated concrete panels and fire/structural specifications remain gaps. Sources: R152.
- concrete-mass-rcc — Concrete · Mass concrete / RCC: Seeded / partial: Preserve detailed mass/thermal research; add pavement RCC. Dam RCC has different construction and performance needs. Sources: R110, R153.
- concrete-pavement-pervious — Concrete · Paving / pervious: Seeded / partial: RCC, recycled-aggregate and pervious pavement seeds complement existing IL paving research. Sources: R153, R154, R174, R135.
- concrete-shotcrete — Concrete · Shotcrete: Seeded / partial: Existing single Type IL wet-mix study retained; broader dry/wet shotcrete, accelerator and overhead qualification remain gaps. Sources: R55.
- concrete-precast-insitu-print — Concrete · Precast / cast in situ / 3D printing: Seeded / partial: Existing precast and lab printing records retained with general in-place curing guidance. Layer bond, reinforcement, geometry and print QA need dedicated sources. Sources: R31, R56, R57, R132, R158.
- concrete-circular — Concrete · Recycled / low-carbon / carbon-cured concrete: Seeded / partial: Recycled aggregate and lower-clinker LCA coverage seeded; carbonatable binders are not proof of performance for every CO2-injected or carbon-cured product. Carbon-cured field trials remain a gap. Sources: R154, R99, R100, R137, R146.
- concrete-polymer-refractory — Concrete · Polymer / polymer-modified / refractory: Seeded / partial: Polymer-concrete preview and CAC refractory FAQ seeded. Polymer-modified hydraulic concrete and refractory installation/thermal cycling require dedicated guides. Sources: R151, R141.
- concrete-architectural — Concrete · Architectural / decorative / exposed aggregate: Seeded / partial: White/colored mortar, discoloration and existing architectural case study seeded; pigments, texture, exposed aggregate and decorative finish specifications need independent references. Sources: R147, R163, R130.
- concrete-repair-grout-overlay — Concrete · Repair mortars / grouts / overlays / cementitious composites: Seeded / partial: Distinguish bonding repair mortars, void-filling grout, low-strength fill and polymer composites. Repair selection, substrate/bond, overlay design and long-term field validation remain thin. Sources: R162, R142, R151, R160.

#### Cross-cutting engineering topics
- cross-chemistry — Cross-cutting · Chemistry / hydration / raw materials / manufacture: Partial coverage: Distinct hydraulic, alkali-activation and carbonation reactions need separate chemistry; raw-material/process datasets remain partial. Sources: R140, R143, R145, R146.
- cross-mix — Cross-cutting · Mix design / aggregates / admixtures / compatibility: Partial coverage: Qualify binder-SCM-admixture-aggregate combinations and source changes; avoid transferring Type IL-specific dosage guidance to all families. Sources: R159, R167, R154, R176.
- cross-construction — Cross-cutting · Production / transport / placement / finishing / curing: Partial coverage: Document delivery adjustments, placement responsibilities and moisture/temperature curing; transport-specific datasets remain thin. Sources: R158, R166, R168.
- cross-mechanics — Cross-cutting · Strength / shrinkage / creep / cracking / thermal behavior: Partial coverage: Strength, curling, plastic shrinkage and mass heat have distinct mechanisms; broad creep and shrinkage constitutive models remain gaps. Sources: R156, R157, R161, R169, R171, R175, R110.
- cross-durability — Cross-cutting · Durability / corrosion / exposure / service life: Partial coverage: Exposure, steel passivation and curing govern durability; do not generalize short laboratory mortar tests to long service life. Sources: R165, R63, R145.
- cross-tests-codes — Cross-cutting · Testing / specifications / codes / QA: Partial coverage: Official catalogue scopes are not full normative text; testing information sheets are not substitutes for adopted ASTM/ACI/EN procedures. Sources: R149, R150, R170, R171, R177.
- cross-failure-repair — Cross-cutting · Failures / field investigations / repairs / case studies: Partial coverage: Retain WDM forensic and aggregate troubleshooting; new-binder field failure and repair case histories remain sparse. Sources: R135, R176, R142.
- cross-environment-cost — Cross-cutting · Environment / LCA / cost: Partial coverage: Compare equivalent function, service life, boundary and region; distinguish project claims and model costs from verified EPDs and market prices. Sources: R99, R100, R137, R143, R145, R146.
- cross-supply-region — Cross-cutting · Availability / supply / regional practice: Partial coverage: Approval lists and local product availability are time-sensitive. No comprehensive regional price series, global classification crosswalk or supply inventory established. Sources: R28, R139, R149, R150, R147.

### Current gaps and evidence policy
- New scope is foundational, not complete: 38 additions do not provide comprehensive coverage of all binders, concrete families or jurisdictions.
- Verification boundary: new PDF text was inspected; web records, abstracts, manufacturer descriptions and standard catalogue scopes are labeled. Original R1–R139 were preserved, not all reverified this pass; R118 authors/year remain unconfirmed.
- Normative access: EN 197-1 and EN 197-5 official catalogue scopes now added (R149–R150), but full official texts still not reviewed. ACI 318/301 primary code coverage remains open. ACI 225R-16 and 548.6R-19 are dated previews, not asserted latest editions.
- High priority gaps: dedicated emerging-SCM qualifications; structural CAC/CSA and geopolymer field approvals; API/ISO current well-cement requirements; carbon-cured/CO2-injected concrete field evidence; AAC panels; dry shotcrete; polymer-modified and refractory practice; ECC and non-synthetic FRC design; architectural/exposed-aggregate guidance; creep and service-life models.
- Commercial/regional gaps: no current regional cement/concrete market cost series, comprehensive local availability inventory or global standards equivalence map. Vendor/project carbon and cost claims are not independent EPDs or market observations.
- Historical gap statements below record what earlier searches had not found, not proof that no such literature or DOT provision exists. Earlier Type IL thermal/finishing rules and single-study conclusions must not be generalized to all cement/concrete families.

### Pass 2 takeaways by topic
- binder-portland: Pass 2 (2026-11-09) historical backfill: NBS Lerch & Bogue 1934 heat of hydration and Flint & Wells 1941 hydrogarnet/sulfate work, Taylor's 1989 Bogue modification, NISTIR 4785 reference-clinker XRD and a 2022 history review (R210, R211, R212, R213, R214). Historic data explain Type II/IV/V logic; current ASTM C150 limits still govern.
- binder-white-masonry: Pass 2: NBS Monograph 36 (1961) shows bond strength dominated wall racking/flexure; repair-mortar guidance for traditional masonry, white clinker defects and LBNL albedo data showing white-cement concrete markedly more reflective (R215, R216, R217, R218). Still no current ASTM C91/C1328/C1329 text reviewed.
- binder-international: Pass 2 / current: EN 197-6:2023 RCF cements (preview), Dutch EN 197 overview incl. NEN 8005/CUR 48 rule, Swiss SIA 215/1 (2025) and SN EN 206 ND (2025) paper, Polish CEM II/C-M & CEM VI concrete data (R206, R207, R208, R249). China GB 175 and India IS 269/1489 still not covered by verified sources.
- concrete-heavyweight: Pass 2: gamma and neutron shielding evidence (barite/magnetite/goethite/serpentine HPC; 2021 neutron and 2024 radiation-shielding reviews; ferrophosphorus weighting for well cement) (R221, R222, R223, R224). Lab/review evidence; shielding design requires project-specific nuclear analysis and ACI 349/NRC-type requirements not reviewed.
- concrete-fibers: Pass 2: Zollo 1997 30-year FRC overview, steel vs macro-synthetic workability/air study and a GFRC review (R225, R226, R227). ACI 544 documents and EN 14651/ASTM C1609 residual-strength methods remain to be reviewed.
- concrete-mass-rcc: Pass 2: 2010 CP Tech Center RCC pavement guide (full PDF), gyratory mix-design procedure and natural-pozzolan RCC scaling study; NBS 1934 heat data also tagged (R204, R210, R228, R229, R230). RCC dam practice (USACE EM 1110-2-2006, USBR) still open; ACI 327 spec expected 2027 per NRMCA report.
- concrete-polymer-refractory: Pass 2: 1973 BNL/USBR concrete-polymer topical report, 1988 polymer concrete mechanics, 2020 polymer-modified mortar comparison (R231, R232, R233). Refractory castable practice still thin; ACI 548 documents not re-reviewed.
- concrete-scc: Pass 2: Okamura & Ouchi originators' papers (2000 fib; 2003 JACT), UT Austin aggregates-in-SCC research, PCI girder bond/transfer length and a formwork-pressure review (R234, R235, R236, R237, R238). ACI 237R and EN 206 Annex G/EFNARC not yet reviewed.
- concrete-architectural: Pass 2: TU Delft historic concrete thesis (Dutch surface finishes), bughole image analysis, LBNL concrete albedo study (R218, R219, R220). ACI 303R architectural cast-in-place guidance and CIB/DIN 18217 surface classes not yet reviewed.
- scm-flyash: Pass 2: Class F durability study, TxDOT 5,500-sample fly ash database and ASR index, ASR-mitigation state-of-art (R209, R239, R240, R241). Harvested/landfilled ash qualification (ASTM C618 updates) and supply data remain gaps.
- scm-limestone: Pass 2: carboaluminate (2001), early filler-strength (1977), 2018 review and limestone-cement sulfate microstructure (2003) studies; also CEM II/C-M/CEM VI data (R209, R242, R243, R244, R245, R249). Mostly DOI-level metadata; full texts closed.
- scm-natural: Pass 2: Roman concrete volcanic ash (2009) and hot-mixing lime clast mechanism (2023), secondary-mineral effects on pozzolanicity (2008), Trass RCC case (R230, R246, R247, R248). ASTM C618 Class N current-edition review still pending.

### Pass 2 gaps
- Pass 2 (2026-11-09) is a second batch, not complete coverage. Many pass-2 records are DOI/abstract-level (closed full text); access level is recorded per record in research/portable/verified-sources.jsonl. ### Current awareness (2026)
- EN 206-1:2026 (CEN, March 2026; R355 preview): EN 206 split into Parts 1–3, superseding EN 206:2013+A2:2021; adds CO2-emission classes. National adoption by Sept 2026.
- ACI CODE-318-25 released Jan 2025 (R356, release news; code text not reviewed). ACI PRC-522-23 pervious concrete report supersedes 522R-10 (R357 preview).
- VTRC 26-R52 (June 2026, R358): VDOT evaluation of LC3 to address fly ash shortage; uses ASTM C1897 R3 reactivity. 2026 journal items: R274, R292, R293, R298, R299, R309, R318, R325, R366.
